PRELIMINARY REVIEW

BLOCKING REVIEW — exact head `7f2011472dbe18d8efdbdff015351c544b7142e0`.

The new `plasmon.ndeploy.json` entry points to `apps/review/review.v0.1.0.neutron`, but the same head packages Review as `review.v0.1.1.neutron`. The packaged demo CI consequently fails in `verifyDeploymentArchives` before the Playwright acceptance: `Required Plasmon deployment archive was not produced: apps/review/review.v0.1.0.neutron`. Update the manifest to the actual supported Review archive/version and rerun the packaged checks. The flake applicability job also fails because `test/ci/select-plasmon-flake-characterization.mjs` is missing on this head; that workflow/integration failure must be reconciled separately before the PR can be considered green.

Review ID: `pr-433-75ad5cc00831-1787623103876-e8655c7b`

### 1. Issue and evidence fully inspected
Read the complete Issue and inspect all evidence before judging the implementation.

- [x] The complete canonical Issue was read, including body, acceptance criteria, comments, links, and dependencies.
  > The complete #429 body and all 11 acceptance criteria were read from the review bundle; the live Issue comments were also fetched.
- [x] Every Issue attachment or linked evidence artifact was inspected, including screenshots, videos, and comparison references.
  > The Issue body contains no screenshot, video, or comparison attachment URLs; that absence was recorded, and the packaged evidence referenced by the PR was inspected through its exact CI log.
- [x] Related Issues, parent/ancestor PRs, and existing accepted behavior were inspected where relevant.
  > Related #466, #110, #189, #174, and #428 contracts/comments were inspected; #110 is merged/satisfied and #466 remains the separate r2 safe-default owner.

### 2. Issue intent, scope, and protected behavior understood
Identify the user problem and intended observable behavior independently of the PR description.

- [x] The user problem and desired observable behavior were stated independently of the PR implementation.
  > The observable goal is a durable global hidden-file preference that changes Search/Start eligibility while composing with Explorer's existing local preference; this was evaluated independently of the implementation.
- [x] Protected behavior, explicit non-goals, and compatibility boundaries were identified.
  > The review identified protected-resource mutation, canonical filesystem/classification authority, local-vs-global preference ownership, and shortcut NodeId preservation as protected boundaries.
- [x] The PR scope matches the Issue intent rather than a narrower or implementation-defined substitute.
  > The final changed-file set implements the requested Settings, Explorer, Search, Start, persistence, deterministic-test, and packaged-test scope without substituting a UI-only filter.

### 3. Release policy and integration context verified
Check release-specific authority, declared bases, stacked dependencies, and which parent work is actually creditable.

- [x] Current assignment, release policy, target branch, and package/version constraints were read.
  > SPECIFIC-REVIEW.md was read: the declared target is release/0.1.0-r2, Plasmon v0.1.0/version 100 is frozen, and the five required r2 gates were identified.
- [x] The declared PR base, stacked-parent relationship, and integration assumptions were verified.
  > PR #433 declares base release/0.1.0-r2 and the exact review bundle records head 75ad5cc008317c7cd6ba6937834960d7efd90cef; no stacked-parent dependency is assumed.
- [x] Only merged or otherwise explicitly creditable parent behavior was counted as implemented.
  > The assessment credits only the current PR head, merged #110/#189/#428 behavior, and exact-head CI; open #466 or other unmerged work is not counted.

### 4. Implementation correctness and failure paths verified
Review success, failure, boundary, asynchronous, cancellation, cleanup, and regression behavior—not only the happy path.

- [x] Success, failure, empty, exceptional, and boundary paths were inspected where applicable.
  > Hidden preference defaults, persistence, global/local combinations, hidden traversal, hidden native projection, hidden/orphan shortcuts, protection, and packaged failure/absence paths were inspected in production code and tests.
- [x] Async ownership, cancellation, teardown, cleanup, error visibility, and resource ownership were inspected where applicable.
  > The store serializes writes with writeChain, mounted flags unsubscribe React listeners, Search owns AbortController cancellation, and Start/Explorer async listings guard stale updates.
- [x] The change does not materially regress unrelated accepted behavior.
  > The exact-head required lanes are green and the diff preserves canonical protected filesystem operations, local FileManager preference storage, and native app composition; no unrelated behavioral regression was found.

### 5. Architecture, authority, and subsystem boundaries preserved
Confirm that behavior remains in the canonical owning layer and does not create parallel authority or cross a product boundary.

- [x] The canonical owning service, model, controller, or adapter remains authoritative.
  > The implementation keeps filesystem metadata as durable preference authority, #189 classifyResource as classification authority, FileManager as local preference owner, and Shell as Search/Start composition.
- [x] Relevant identity, filesystem, Neutron, Process, Windowing, Shell, security, or other subsystem boundaries remain intact.
  > NodeId targets are validated with fs.stat, native/.neutron projections are resolved from canonical filesystem paths, and Neutron/Process/Windowing responsibilities remain outside the new preference policy.
- [x] No duplicate authority, hidden parallel implementation, or convenience architecture was introduced.
  > HiddenVisibilityPreferenceStore is the single global store injected through the composition root; no localStorage/IndexedDB or surface-specific shadow store was added.

### 6. Tests are honest, deterministic, and sufficient
Tests must observe production behavior at the lowest truthful layer and must not be weakened or made circular.

- [x] Tests assert user-visible or contract behavior rather than source shape, incidental structure, or constants alone.
  > The new deterministic tests assert persisted values, visibility results, shortcut identity, protection rejection, and all local/global combinations rather than source strings.
- [x] Tests use the lowest honest layer with deterministic control and appropriate negative/boundary cases.
  > Headless production composition covers deterministic policy and the Playwright test covers installed UI/browser behavior; cancellation, missing targets, hidden directories, and negative states are included.
- [x] Fixtures, examples, tolerances, and bounds match the Issue rather than being relaxed to fit the implementation.
  > Fixtures use actual hidden files/directories, .Properties.sys, real shortcut NodeIds, and the installed Settings/Explorer flow; assertions are not relaxed geometry or source-shape checks.

### 7. Runtime, packaged, browser, and manual evidence verified
Use real packaged/browser/manual evidence whenever the claim depends on layout, assets, runtime, persistence, or visual parity.

- [x] The required evidence layer for the Issue was identified correctly.
  > The Issue requires installed/browser evidence for Settings-to-Explorer/Search/Start behavior and strict BrowserHealth, so the packaged specialist lane is the correct evidence layer.
- [ ] Packaged, browser, runtime, persistence, or human/manual evidence was inspected where the claim requires it.
  > :x: The exact packaged test passed, but its global-ON section asserts only that Search reveals Properties; it never opens/observes Start while the global setting is ON, so the required packaged Start positive transition remains unverified.
- [x] Execution evidence is distinguished from CI status and is not replaced by a green status label.
  > The specialist log shows 28 tests passed including the #429 file, and the bundle records green Fast Bun, persistence, smoke, Kernel, and 10/10 plus 50/50 flake evidence; this is distinguished from source correctness.

### 8. Compatibility, regressions, documentation, and release obligations reviewed
Check durable state, compatibility, scope, documentation, generated artifacts, and applicable release obligations.

- [x] Durable state, persistence, migration, serialized contracts, and upgrade/restart behavior were reviewed where applicable.
  > The preference is a namespaced root metadata patch, not a schema replacement; reconstruction tests verify global and local values survive service recreation and installed reload.
- [x] Required architecture, API, developer-facing, persistence, or integration documentation was reviewed or updated where applicable.
  > The PR updates the affected README documentation fingerprints and the reviewed code retains the filesystem, Shell, Explorer, and testing authority documentation.
- [x] Scope, generated artifacts, dependency changes, release obligations, and unrelated work were reviewed.
  > The complete bundle's final changed-file list is bounded to #429 implementation/tests plus six documentation fingerprints and one related chrome assertion; no version bump or unrelated dependency update is required by r2 policy.

### 9. Exact-head and reviewer-operational disposition verified
The formal disposition must be bound to the current exact head and must follow reviewer independence and reporting rules.

- [x] The exact PR head and declared base were recorded and refreshed immediately before output.
  > The immediate queue refresh still reports PR #433 COMPLETE at head 75ad5cc008317c7cd6ba6937834960d7efd90cef against release/0.1.0-r2.
- [x] The reviewer did not implement product changes, merge, force-push, or alter another agent's work.
  > This session only inspected the exact PR, Issue, tests, and CI; it did not edit product code, merge, force-push, or alter another agent's work.
- [x] CI status and failures are recorded as merge/infrastructure evidence, not used as product-correctness proof.
  > CI was treated as separate gate/evidence: exact specialist logs and the bundled required-check results were inspected rather than used as a substitute for acceptance analysis.

### 10. Acceptance criteria represented in production code and tests
Every Issue acceptance criterion must have production implementation and at least one honest executable test in this PR or an already-merged or pending-merge parent branch. Each criterion below comes directly from the linked Issue.

- [x] Durable global preference exists and defaults OFF.
  > The root metadata store, OFF default, and reconstruction path are implemented and exercised by the focused persistence test.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > HiddenVisibilityPreferenceStore validates versioned root metadata, defaults false, serializes updates, and is injected from services.ts.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > apps/plasmon/src/os/hiddenVisibility.test.ts asserts default false, writes true, disposes, reconstructs, and reads true.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The test observes FsService-backed values across service reconstruction, not a constant or source string.

- [x] Global OFF preserves #466 Start/Search safe-default behavior.
  > OFF is threaded into Search/Start and the tests assert hidden files, directories, Properties, and hidden-target shortcuts are absent.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > searchFilesystem lists with includeHidden false and listVisibleStartMenuFolder does the same when the persisted global value is false.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The focused shell hiddenVisibility test asserts OFF exclusion for ordinary hidden resources, Properties projection, and a shortcut targeting a hidden file.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > Those assertions inspect returned production Search/Start result nodes and IDs, including negative results, rather than source structure.

- [x] Global ON makes hidden resources eligible in Start/Search through canonical classification/target resolution.
  > ON enables hidden filesystem traversal and canonical target checks, and focused tests cover hidden files, nested hidden directories, Properties, and Start shortcuts.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > ON passes includeHidden true and applies fs.stat/classified /System or /Apps resolution before allowing native, element, or node targets.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The shell test turns the store ON and asserts hidden files/directories/shortcut targets and exactly one Properties result, while its Start case asserts hidden targets reappear.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > Assertions inspect actual SearchBatch results and Start folder nodes from the headless production service graph.

- [x] Explorer local visibility alone never changes Start/Search.
  > Explorer-local state is kept in FileManagerPreferenceStore and is not read by Search/Start; the installed test exercises local ON with global OFF.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > Search/Start read only HIDDEN_VISIBILITY_PREFERENCES_KEY, while Explorer uses its separate FileManager preference plus the global OR composition.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The packaged journey checks local Explorer ON, then asserts Properties remains absent from both Search and Start while global remains OFF.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The browser assertions observe the real installed surfaces and the focused tests inspect separate persisted stores.

- [x] Global ON forces Explorer effective visibility true and renders its local checkbox checked + disabled.
  > Explorer computes global OR local visibility and disables its local checkbox when the global value is true; packaged evidence observes checked/disabled state.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > ExplorerApp uses effectiveShowHiddenFiles = alwaysShowHiddenFiles || viewPreferences.showHiddenFiles and disabled={alwaysShowHiddenFiles}.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The packaged test checks the local box, enables the global box, and asserts the local control is checked and disabled.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The test observes rendered checkbox state and the FileManager list's .Properties.sys entry, not a helper constant.

- [x] Global ON -> OFF restores the prior local #110 preference and editable control.
  > Global OFF leaves the FileManager preference untouched and re-enables the local control; both focused combination tests and packaged assertions cover this.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > Explorer never writes the local preference when global mode changes; it derives effectiveShowHiddenFiles and only the local checkbox handler calls FileManagerPreferenceStore.save.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The focused test saves local true, toggles global on/off, and verifies local true; the packaged test repeats the rendered transition.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The evidence reads persisted local state and rendered control state after actual toggles.

- [x] Hidden native `.sys` projection and shortcut-target visibility use canonical hidden state rather than UI heuristics.
  > Native and shortcut paths resolve canonical resources and use filesystem listing/stat hiddenness; focused tests cover Properties, native shortcuts, node shortcuts, and orphan targets.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > findSystemAppResource/findNeutronAppResource use classifyResource and isNodeEligibleForHiddenVisibility validates fs.stat plus canonical parent listing.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The shell tests assert no duplicate Properties result, native Properties shortcut filtering, hidden node-target filtering, hidden-directory traversal, and deleted-target filtering.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > Tests inspect Search/Start result kinds and stable NodeIds, including the orphan shortcut regression, rather than dot-prefix heuristics.

- [x] Protection semantics are unchanged.
  > Global visibility only changes listing/presentation and the focused test confirms protected Properties rename remains rejected.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The new store does not alter ProtectedManagedFsService/resourceCapabilities; Explorer wraps only list visibility.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > hiddenVisibility.test.ts enables the preference and expects renaming /System/.Properties.sys to reject with protected.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > The test performs the real protected FsService operation and checks its error, not a source-level guard.

- [x] Focused tests cover persistence and all global/local preference combinations.
  > Focused coverage includes default/persistence, all four global/local combinations, and reconstruction.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > Production code provides versioned global and existing versioned local filesystem-backed stores.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The focused hiddenVisibility test covers false/true global values, local false/true combinations, and reopened repository state.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > Assertions observe loaded values and composeExplorerHiddenVisibility outputs derived from actual preference cases.

- [ ] Packaged-browser acceptance proves Settings -> Search/Start/FileManager transitions using a known hidden resource.
  > :x: The installed test covers Search and FileManager positive/negative transitions and Start while OFF, but omits the required installed Start assertion while global visibility is ON.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The production path is wired through Settings -> shared store -> fs events -> Search/Start/Explorer, with canonical resource projection.
    - [ ] An executable test covers it.
      > :x: test/e2e/plasmon-hidden-visibility-429.spec.ts exercises the installed journey but never asserts that Start renders Properties after globalHidden.check(); only Search is checked in the ON state.
    - [ ] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > :x: The existing browser assertions are truthful for the states they cover, but they do not observe the missing global-ON Start behavior required by this criterion.

- [x] BrowserHealth remains strict.
  > The packaged test installs BrowserHealth and calls health.assertClean after the real journey.
    - [x] Production code represents the behavior.
      > The browser test installs strict BrowserHealth with only the narrowly bounded Kernel iframe warning allowance.
    - [x] An executable test covers it.
      > The exact specialist run executed the #429 Playwright test and reported it passed.
    - [x] The test observes behavior rather than source shape.
      > health.assertClean() is an executable runtime assertion; the allowance is exact message plus /chunks/ path and does not broadly ignore warnings.

### Summary
> Approval is allowed only when every checkbox above is checked. CI status is recorded separately and is not used as proof that the Issue is solved.
